adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:3 — [P1|conf50] `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids` omits `include: true`, so AMS emits only `embeddable_host_ids` and never sideloads an `embeddable_hosts` root — exactly what store.js.es6:168 reads — leaving every host object `undefined`.

If `_lookupSubType` can’t find a referenced record (e.g., an id is missing from the sideloaded payload), it will return `undefined`/`null`, and the resulting array will contain `undefined` entries. The `hydrated || []` fallback is ineffective because `map` always returns an array (truthy), so you won’t get an empty list or an error—just an array with undefined elements. `EmbeddingSerializer` uses `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids`, which is exactly the codepath that triggers the new `*_ids` hydration logic.

In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural-ids branch (`if (m[2])`) always runs `obj[k].map(...)`, assigns the result to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]`, and then `delete obj[k]` unconditionally. Since `Array#map` always returns an array, `hydrated || []` will never fall back, and any `_lookupSubType` miss will produce `undefined` entries in the array. Unlike the singular branch (which only deletes the original `*_id` when a hydrated object exists), the plural branch will always remove the original `*_ids` even when hydration fails, losing the raw IDs and replacing them with `[undefined, ...]`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:192 — [P2|conf75] the shared hydrator regex was widened app-wide from `/(.+)\_id$/` to `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` for one admin page, so any unrelated rest_serializer payload carrying `*_ids` without a matching sideloaded collection now silently loses its raw ids.
